thread:
ravi: Quick sync on autoscale admission policy for Dedicated pools. I want to lock down the speculative warmup margin behavior so operator vs control-plane responsibilities are clear. Proposal: operator can speculatively provision up to `speculative_margin` slots beyond an active lease to reduce tail latency, BUT it must register those as `speculative` and they must be reclaimed first on cost pressure.

elaine: Important to specify how speculative slots affect billing and tenant accounting. They should not count against runway budgets, but we should tag them in audit so billing can treat them as operator-driven optimizations.

peter: Risk: speculative provisioning across many tenants could create a capacity stampede. We need a global soft cap and per-tenant cap. Suggest config: `speculative_margin_per_lease`, `speculative_global_cap_percent`. Operator refuses to speculatively provision if global usage > cap.

ravi: Agreed. Also add a decay window: once speculative slots are created, if they're unused for `speculative_idle_seconds`, operator should tear them down. Keeps waste bounded.

elaine: For visibility: emit metrics `speculative_slots_created_total`, `speculative_slots_reclaimed_total`, `speculative_idle_seconds_histogram`. Add tenant label. Also emit an event when speculative provisioning was prevented due to global cap.

peter: Admission circuit detail: when a request arrives and runway is exhausted, operator should attempt a single speculative provision attempt only if tenant has recent healthy traffic (e.g., success_rate over last minute > 80%) to avoid gaming. Otherwise route to fallback.

ravi: Good guardrail. Pseudoconfig snippet: ```
speculation_policy:
  speculative_margin_per_lease: 1
  speculative_global_cap_percent: 7
  speculative_idle_seconds: 45
  min_recent_success_rate: 0.8
```

elaine: Implementation note: speculative nodes must be labeled in orchestration metadata so cost managers can exclude them from committed capacity tallies. Also operator must expose an API to list speculative allocations per tenant for debugging.

peter: Failure modes: if operator creates speculative nodes but kube/cloud fails to schedule them, it should fallback to quick hosted attempt (short TTL). We'll log `speculative_failure` with error codes.

infra-bot: rollout plan: speculation-policy v1 -> feature-flagged on staging -> collect metrics 48h -> small beta on 5 tenants -> evaluate cost delta -> prod gate.

ravi: Action items: (1) I'll add policy fields + failure semantics to RFC. (2) @elaine will add metric names and a logging event schema. (3) @peter will sketch operator checks and the per-tenant recent-traffic heuristic.

elaine: I'll also make sure audit entries include `speculative_marker` and `reclaim_reason` so finance can reconcile.

ravi: Thanks. Keeping speculation bounded and observable should reduce tail latencies without surprising cost.
